label: Lithium Carbonate (China spot)
delta: Rebounded from 3-month low ¥151,750 (Jun 29) to ¥165,000 (Jul 13), settling ~¥154,000 by Jul 15
deltaNote: Lithium carbonate hit a three-month low of ¥151,750/tonne on June 29, 2026 before rebounding to ¥165,000 by July 13 on stronger-than-expected demand from EV and energy-storage battery makers, then easing to trade flat around ¥154,000 (~$21,500/tonne) by July 15. Volatility continues to reflect thin liquidity and the tug-of-war between new mine supply and accelerating storage demand.

deltaNote: CATL signed a 5 GWh TENER Sodium storage deal with Dutch integrator Alfen on July 16, 2026 — the first planned sodium-ion BESS deployment in Europe — adding to its 60 GWh HyperStrong domestic order. Separately, peer-reviewed research published Jun 21 found Chinese maker Hina's sodium-ion cells, using a tabless double-aluminum current collector design, now match Tesla's lithium-ion cells on manufacturing quality and performance — a notable validation of sodium-ion's production maturity, not just its cost story.

deltaNote: CATL's 1st-gen Shenxing (2024) achieved 4C; Qilin 3 claims 10C continuous with 3,000 kW output — enabling ~400 km recovered in under 5 minutes. Targets 1,000+ km WLTP range in premium vehicle platform. If achieved commercially, eliminates fast-charging as an EV objection.
